newsitem.title: USA: Applied Magnetics calls off Read-Rite bid.
newsitem.headline: Applied Magnetics calls off Read-Rite bid.

text.p: Applied Magnetics Corp., whose stock has tumbled in recent weeks, said Friday it was withdrawing its hostile bid to acquire Read-Rite Corp. because of the stock decline.

"Although we continue to believe the strategic rationale for this combination is compelling, we recognise that based on the current value of Applied Magnetics' common stock the transaction is not feasible," Chief Executive Craig Crisman said in a statement.
Trading in Applied Magnetics' stock, which jumped up immediately after the announcement, was later halted by the New York Stock Exchange because of an order imbalance.
The shares had added $1.375 to $34.75 before the halt.
However, less than a month ago, the stock traded at $60.50.
Read-Rite, also a maker of disk drive components, said a combination with Applied would interfere with its strategy for the future and had turned down the bid.

Shares of Applied Magnetics fell $5 to $33.25 in extremely heavy trading Thursday after the Montgomery Securities brokerage lowered its fiscal 1997 revenue estimate for the maker of computer disk drive heads.

The stock's sharp drop extended a substantial decline that began with the company's Feb. 24 announcement of a hostile takeover bid for Read-Rite Corp. in which Applied Magnetics intended to use its stock to complete the purchase.
When it was announced, the offer to swap 0.679 Applied share for each Read-Rite share was worth $1.8 billion -- based on an Applied Magnetics share price of $55.25 as of the Feb. 21 market close.
The three-week tumble wiped out a spectacular rise in Applied Magnetic's stock over the first six weeks of 1997.
